entries.what: API version 2025-10 stopped being accessible at 15:00 UTC on October 16, 2026. A request naming it does not fail outright. Shopify falls forward and answers at the oldest accessible stable version, 2026-01 today, and the X-Shopify-API-Version response header then differs from the version asked for. Webhook payloads fall forward the same way. So the break is silent: shapes change under the code, a GraphQL selection of something removed since its version returns an error, and REST fields go missing. Polaris UI extensions are different: the page says older versions keep working, without reference docs, and Shopify CLI refuses to deploy a version older than 12 months. A public app still using unsupported resources after the upgrade deadline is also delisted from the App Store.

source.quote: 2025-10 | October 1, 2025 | October 16, 2026 15:00 UTC | Unsupported

lookFor: 2025-10 in a REST or GraphQL path: /admin/api/<version>/..., /api/<version>/graphql.json, /customer/api/<version>/graphql

2025-10 set as apiVersion, api_version, API_VERSION, SHOPIFY_API_VERSION or a Session argument, or named by the ApiVersion enum of @shopify/shopify-api. A bare version setting can belong to another vendor, so check it is Shopify. A date-versioned string with a day, such as 2024-10-21, is not this.
2025-10 in a REST resources import, @shopify/shopify-api/rest/admin/<version>. Its classes send /admin/api/<version>/... whatever version the app config sets.
api_version in shopify.app.toml (webhooks fall forward). In shopify.extension.toml a UI extension's api_version isn't a break by itself: see what.
entries.replacement: 2026-10, the latest stable version the page lists. Accessible until October 16, 2027 15:00 UTC.
requires: The app already runs at 2026-01 by falling forward, so these are the changes the move to 2026-10 adds. Read each version crossed: https://shopify.dev/changelog/release-notes/2026-04, https://shopify.dev/changelog/release-notes/2026-07, https://shopify.dev/changelog/release-notes/2026-10. A pin below 2026-01 also has code written for an older shape: https://shopify.dev/changelog/release-notes/2026-01 lists Shop.draftOrders removed, groupObjects dropped from bulkOperationRunMutation, and cartDiscountCodesUpdate now requiring discountCodes.

2026-04: inventorySetQuantities, inventoryAdjustQuantities, inventoryMoveQuantities, inventorySetOnHandQuantities and productVariantsBulkUpdate must send changeFromQuantity (the expected quantity, or null to opt out). Remove compareQuantity and ignoreCompareQuantity.

2026-04: the notes say idempotency is mandatory for specific mutations, naming inventory adjustments and refunds. inventoryAdjustQuantities takes its required key through the @idempotent directive; read each mutation reference for the others, since a missing key fails the call.

2026-04: FulfillmentService.permitsSkuSharing is gone, including from fulfillmentServiceCreate and fulfillmentServiceUpdate. inventoryActivate no longer defaults available or onHand to zero when they are omitted.
2026-04 webhooks: checkouts/create and checkouts/update lose id (use token), and orders/* topics lose checkout_id (use checkout_token).

2026-07: inventorySetScheduledChanges is removed with no replacement. Replace DraftOrderLineItem.grams with weight, which returns value and unit. visibleToStorefrontApi is removed from MetaobjectFieldDefinition and its create and update inputs. Collections move to Collection.sources from only Collection.ruleSet.

2026-10: changing the shipping address on an unfulfilled order with orderUpdate or the REST order update endpoint now recalculates taxes. Re-read taxLines, totalTaxSet and totals afterward and handle the balance difference.

2026-10: DraftOrderDiscountNotAppliedWarning.priceRule and the PriceRule object are removed from the GraphQL schema: select discountTitle and discountCode. Segment query functions use MATCHES and NOT MATCHES instead of = true and = false. A query filtering by a metafield that is not valid for filtering now returns an error. CustomerPhoneNumber.smsMarketingConsent replaces the flat SMS consent fields, and checkout and customer account UI extension metafield declarations need an owner_type. Carrier services no longer add rates to the General shipping profile by default.

Webhook payloads follow the subscription version, so change [webhooks] api_version in shopify.app.toml or the subscription too, and read handlers against the new shape. After the move, check the X-Shopify-API-Version response header equals the version asked for.
Code naming the version by the ApiVersion enum needs an @shopify package new enough to hold that value. This is a reading: the page does not say it.

The lighter path: passing the version as a plain string, apiVersion: "2026-10", needs no package upgrade. @shopify/shopify-api 11.0.0 and 12.2.0 hand the value through unchecked (lib/clients/admin/rest/client.ts in https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js), and a test with a mocked fetch saw it reach /admin/api/2026-10/ for GraphQL and REST. That is SDK behaviour, not a Shopify promise: it shows what the SDK sends, not what Shopify answers, so check the X-Shopify-API-Version response header. TypeScript needs a cast, since the config's type is the ApiVersion enum.

A REST resources import, @shopify/shopify-api/rest/admin/<version>, pins its classes to that version whatever the app config sets, so it has to move too. The folder must ship in the package: 15.0.1 stops at rest/admin/2026-07 and 12.2.0 at rest/admin/2025-10. This is read from the packages, not from Shopify's page.

A UI extension's api_version in shopify.extension.toml moves with its @shopify/ui-extensions package: Shopify's upgrade guide changes both, api_version = "2026-04" with @shopify/ui-extensions 2026.4.x (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/checkout-ui-extensions/2026-10/upgrading-to-2026-10). Older Polaris extensions keep working, so don't bump an extension's api_version alone.

entries.what: The Storefront API Checkout mutations are shut off, so a checkout can't be created or completed through them. The migration guide names checkoutCreate, checkoutLineItemsReplace, checkoutCustomerAssociateV2, checkoutDiscountCodeApplyV2, checkoutShippingAddressUpdateV2 and checkoutUserErrors. The other names here come from the mutation files in Shopify's own js-buy-sdk at v2.22.0, not from the page. Their reference pages return 404 at 2026-01. The JS Buy SDK and Buy Button had a later grace period: see SH-3.

source.quote: are deprecated and will be shut off on April 1, 2025

lookFor: A GraphQL document or helper calling one of these checkout mutations, or reading checkoutUserErrors. checkoutCreate can also be an app function of its own name, so check it is a Storefront API call. cartCreate, cartLinesAdd and checkoutUrl are the replacement, not this.
entries.replacement: The Storefront Cart API. The page also offers Checkout Sheet Kit for mobile apps.
requires: Guide with before and after requests: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/headless/building-with-the-storefront-api/cart/migrate-to-cart-api/migrate-your-app.
cartCreate replaces checkoutCreate, and input lines carry merchandiseId where line items carried variantId.
cartLinesUpdate behaves like checkoutLineItemsReplace, and cartLinesAdd adds to what is there. They take a cartId, so store that instead of the checkout id.
Send the buyer to cart.checkoutUrl: the cart does not complete a purchase itself.
Errors come back as userErrors, not checkoutUserErrors.
cartDiscountCodesUpdate takes stackable codes, unlike checkoutDiscountCodeApplyV2.

entries.what: The REST Admin API Checkout endpoints are shut off. The Abandoned checkouts resource (GET checkouts.json and checkouts/count.json) is excepted and still works.

source.quote: are deprecated and will be shut off on April 1, 2025

lookFor: A call under /admin/api/<version>/checkouts/<token>, or a POST or PUT to checkouts.json. A GET of checkouts.json or checkouts/count.json is Abandoned checkouts and is not a break.
entries.replacement: The Storefront Cart API. The page also offers Checkout Sheet Kit for mobile apps.
requires: The Cart API is GraphQL only and client or server side, so a REST call becomes a Storefront API call with a Storefront token: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/headless/building-with-the-storefront-api/cart/migrate-to-cart-api.
Send the buyer to cart.checkoutUrl: the cart does not complete a purchase itself.

entries.what: JS Buy SDK before v3.0 can't complete purchases: its .checkout interface sat on the Checkout APIs. v3.0, the last version, keeps working on Cart API for most uses, with limits, and is deprecated.

source.quote: Critical Deadline: July 1, 2025 11:00 AM ET

lookFor: shopify-buy below 3.0.0 in package.json, or the js-buy-sdk CDN script at a version other than v3. An import or ShopifyBuy.buildClient only counts once the installed version is below 3.0.0: read the lockfile.
entries.replacement: JS Buy SDK v3.0 or the Storefront API Client. The page offers both and says to choose what suits: upgrading to v3.0 extends the grace period, and the Storefront API Client is the other option.
requires: The Storefront API Client is the @shopify/storefront-api-client package. It sends queries: there is no client.checkout interface, so calls become Cart API operations. The changelog post links the migration guide.
The v3.0 stopgap replaces .checkout with a Cart-based equivalent with limits inherent to the Cart API. Check the use case against its upgrade guide before relying on it.

entries.what: Buy Button JS below v3.0 can't complete purchases: it sat on the Checkout APIs.

source.quote: checkout functionality will stop working on older versions of Buy Button JS on August 1, 2025 11:00 AM ET

lookFor: @shopify/buy-button-js below 3 in package.json, or a numbered path under sdks.shopifycdn.com/buy-button/. The latest path is fine.
entries.replacement: The latest major version of Buy Button JS (v3.0).
requires: npm: set @shopify/buy-button-js to ^3.0.4. Script tag: replace the version in the sdks.shopifycdn.com/buy-button path with latest. Steps: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/headless/additional-sdks/buy-button#using-the-latest-version.

entries.what: checkout.liquid and additional scripts are sunset for the Thank you and Order status pages. The page also calls checkout.liquid unsupported for the Information, Shipping and Payment steps, and gives no date for those. A committed layout normally renders all of them, so the date here is the only one the page gives.

source.quote: checkout.liquid and additional scripts were sunset for the Thank you and Order status pages on August 28, 2025

lookFor: A file named checkout.liquid, usually layout/checkout.liquid, or a reference to one.
Liquid objects that only exist in that layout: checkout_scripts, checkout_stylesheets, content_for_order_summary, alternative_payment_methods.
Additional-scripts JavaScript reading Shopify.Checkout.step, Shopify.Checkout.page or Shopify.Checkout.OrderStatus.
entries.replacement: Shopify Extensions in Checkout, as the page says.
requires: This is a rebuild, not an edit: the Liquid layout has no in-place equivalent. Start from https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/checkout/technologies.

For the Thank you and Order status pages, UI goes to customer account UI extensions, which only work on upgraded stores, and tracking goes to web pixels, which work on any store but cannot render UI: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/online-store/script-tag-deprecation/order-status.

entries.what: Shopify Scripts no longer run: Scripts still published on a store were deactivated. The repo's Ruby source then does nothing. Editing and publishing stopped on April 15, 2026, per https://shopify.dev/changelog/shopify-scripts-will-be-deprecated-on-june-30-2026.

source.quote: As of June 30, 2026, Shopify Scripts has been deprecated.

lookFor: A Ruby file that reads Input.cart, Input.shipping_rates or Input.payment_gateways and assigns the matching Output. The same words elsewhere are not this.
entries.replacement: Shopify Functions, through an installed app built on Functions or a custom build.
requires: A Function is not the Ruby script moved over: it is a separate app extension built and deployed through an app, so the logic is rewritten rather than edited in place.
The Shopify Scripts customizations report in the admin lists which customizations can move to Functions or public apps.
Several product discounts on one cart line need DiscountAutomaticBasic.combinesWith set: https://shopify.dev/changelog/release-notes/2026-04.
Custom Functions-based apps must be created through the Dev Dashboard and then connected to the store: apps created in the Shopify admin lack the App Bridge support Functions-based apps need.

entries.what: scriptTagCreate and scriptTagUpdate return an error, and POST and PUT to the ScriptTag REST resource fail, on every API version. Pinning an older version doesn't defer it. Reads and deletes keep working, and existing script tags run until March 1, 2027: see the future entry SH-6.storefront-script-tags.

source.quote: You can't create or update script tags.

lookFor: A call to scriptTagCreate or scriptTagUpdate.
A POST or PUT to /script_tags.json or /script_tags/<id>.json. A GET or DELETE on that path still works and is not a break.
entries.replacement: An app embed block, shipped in a theme app extension. For analytics or conversion data, the page says use a web pixel instead.
requires: An app embed block is enabled per theme by the merchant in the theme editor, so an install no longer turns the script on by itself: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/online-store/theme-app-extensions/migrate.

entries.what: Script tags with a display_scope of order_status or all no longer run on the Order status page: since August 28, 2025 for Plus stores and August 26, 2026 for all others. Apps have not been able to create them since February 1, 2025.

lookFor: A script tag created with display_scope order_status or all, or displayScope ORDER_STATUS or ALL. The value all can be some other setting, so check it is a script tag.
entries.replacement: Customer account UI extensions to render content, and web pixels to track analytics, conversions or customer behavior.
requires: Web pixels work on any store but cannot render UI. Customer account UI extensions can, but only on upgraded stores, so a visual customization has no replacement until the store upgrades.

entries.what: The Global Catalog REST API (Catalog API) has stopped serving traffic.

source.quote: stops serving traffic on November 2, 2026

lookFor: A call to discover.shopifyapps.com, such as /global/v2/search.
entries.replacement: Global Catalog MCP, which implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP).
requires: The endpoint moves to https://catalog.shopify.com/api/ucp/mcp and speaks MCP, with tools search_catalog, lookup_catalog and get_product. Request and response shapes follow the UCP specification, so parsing changes too: https://shopify.dev/docs/agents/catalog/global-catalog.
Every request must include a meta.ucp-agent.profile URL pointing to an agent profile.
A saved catalog no longer has its own endpoint URL: pass its ID as catalog.catalog_id.

entries.what: The metafieldDelete mutation is gone from the GraphQL Admin API from 2025-01. No version gate: every request now runs at 2026-01 or later, because older pins fall forward, so this fails whatever the code pins. Its reference page returns 404 at 2026-01.

source.quote: As of 2025-01 the metafieldDelete Admin API method is being removed.

lookFor: A GraphQL document calling metafieldDelete. metafieldsDelete is the replacement and is not this.
entries.replacement: metafieldsDelete, as the page lists it.
requires: The input changes shape: metafieldsDelete takes an array of identifiers made of ownerId, namespace and key. The page says the Metafield GID is not an option, so code holding only the GID must first read or keep the owner, namespace and key.
The payload returns deletedMetafields, each with key, namespace and ownerId, so code reading the old payload changes too.

entries.what: PrivateMetafield is gone from the GraphQL Admin API from 2025-01. No version gate: every request now runs at 2026-01 or later, because older pins fall forward. The privateMetafieldUpsert and privateMetafieldDelete reference pages return 404 at 2026-01.

entries.replacement: App-data metafields. Where the metafield is needed per resource, the page points to app-reserved namespaces.
requires: Data already stored as private metafields has to be read out or rewritten in the new namespace. The page does not give a copy path, so check the migration guide it links.

entries.what: Shopify no longer sets the _shopify_y and _shopify_s cookies on merchant storefronts, so a read returns nothing. For Hydrogen the dev docs give April 30, 2026, spelled shopify_y and shopify_s, and say a storefront keeps working but visitor and session attribution stops being reliable. The date here is the earlier of the two.

source.quote: Starting on January 1st, 2026 Shopify will no longer set the following cookies on merchant storefronts

lookFor: _shopify_y or _shopify_s read from document.cookie or a cookie library. shopify_y and shopify_s without the underscore are the Hydrogen spelling, and a project could use those names itself, so check.
entries.replacement: For _shopify_y, the clientId property of a Standard or DOM event in Web Pixels. For _shopify_s the page says Shopify will not offer a replacement value, and a session-length cookie of your own is equivalent. On Hydrogen, uniqueToken replaces _y and visitToken replaces _s.
requires: Cookie reads have no drop-in equivalent: the value moves to an API that may be asynchronous or only available in a pixel, so the code around the read changes too. This is a reading of the replacement pages.
event.clientId exists only inside a web pixel, so code outside a pixel has to move into one, and it needs customer consent.
Hydrogen on Oxygen: run the Hydrogen CLI upgrade command. Other hosts: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/headless/hydrogen/migrate/cookies.

future.what: Public apps on non-expiring offline access tokens: delisted and blocked from new installs on January 1, 2027, merchants warned from January 15, and Admin API requests return HTTP 403 from April 1, 2027. The date is the 403. An earlier May 2026 post said authentication errors from January 1. The October 2026 post replaces that. Custom apps and apps created by merchants are excluded.
future.replacement: Expiring offline access tokens. Set expiring to 1 on the token exchange or authorization code grant.
requires: A public app sending expiring=1 is fine, and a custom app is excluded, so read the grant call and the app type.

The token now expires in 60 minutes, and it comes with a refresh_token that lasts 90 days when issued. So token storage needs the new fields, and background jobs and webhooks need a server-side refresh before each use: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/authentication-authorization/access-tokens.
Existing installs migrate in code, with no merchant reinstall. Shopify's app templates and official API libraries already handle refresh.
